The post Oil Prices Drop by Over $1 Per Barrel appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Global oil prices have further decreased. As of 1 AM Bangladesh time on Thursday night, Brent crude prices fell by $1.29 per barrel, or 1.5 percent, to $87.69. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil prices decreased by $1.30, or 1.6 percent, to $81.97.

Qatari-based news agency Al Jazeera reported this information.

Analysts believe that global oil demand might decrease due to the ongoing tensions involving Iran, the United States, and Israel. For this reason, the forecast for global oil demand in 2026 has been lowered.

However, a potential crisis in oil supply stemming from the same conflict is preventing a further significant drop in market prices.

In its monthly oil market report published on Wednesday, OPEC lowered its forecast for global oil demand growth in 2026 to 580,000 barrels per day.

item.title: International Oil Prices See Significant Jump
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Uncertainty over a ceasefire agreement between Iran and the United States, coupled with new attacks on ships in the Middle East, has escalated concerns about global energy supply. As a…

The post International Oil Prices See Significant Jump appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Uncertainty over a ceasefire agreement between Iran and the United States, coupled with new attacks on ships in the Middle East, has escalated concerns about global energy supply. As a result, international oil prices surged again on Wednesday (August 12).

A Reuters report stated that on Wednesday, Brent crude prices in the Asian market rose by 72 cents, or 0.81 percent, to $89.63 per barrel. Concurrently, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil prices increased by 71 cents, or 0.85 percent, to $83.91.

This comes after both benchmarks had risen by more than one dollar on Tuesday, pushing oil prices to their highest level since July 31. On Monday, oil prices had already climbed by nearly 5 percent amid diminishing prospects for a peace deal.

Obstructions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab have become a major cause for concern regarding supply conditions in the Middle East. On Tuesday, the United States and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen separately reported attacks on ships in these two waterways.

Iran’s top security official, Mohsen Rezaee, stated that the crucial Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the United States accepts Iran’s conditions for ending the war. Iran’s demands include the release of its seized assets and the cessation of other conflicts in the Middle East.

According to Reuters shipping data, only six vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, compared to an average of approximately 11 vessels over the preceding 10 days. Before the war, an average of 125 to 140 ships used this waterway daily.

US Crude Oil Inventories Increase

Meanwhile, data indicating a rise in US crude oil inventories has also entered the market. Citing information from the American Petroleum Institute (API), market-related sources reported that US crude oil stockpiles increased by approximately 9.1 million barrels in the week ending August 7.

Conversely, during the same period, gasoline inventories in the country decreased by approximately 1.5 million barrels, and distillate inventories fell by 596,000 barrels.

This increase in crude oil inventories is significantly higher than anticipated. Analysts believe that if confirmed by official government data, this could partially alleviate market concerns about supply shortages.

The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) is scheduled to release official inventory data at 10:30 AM local time on Wednesday.

However, long-term concerns about supply conditions persist. According to EIA forecasts, a deficit of approximately 600,000 barrels per day in crude oil supply from the Middle East could continue until the end of 2027.

Consequently, if the Iran-US conflict is not resolved swiftly and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz does not return to normal, there remains a risk of further increases in international oil prices.

item.title: Nation’s Strength Lies in People’s Economic Empowerment: Prime Minister
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that a nation becomes strong when its people’s economic capability is ensured. No state can be strong by keeping its common people in poverty or…

The post Nation’s Strength Lies in People’s Economic Empowerment: Prime Minister appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that a nation becomes strong when its people’s economic capability is ensured. No state can be strong by keeping its common people in poverty or by silencing them. The Prime Minister also commented that the government’s goal is to lead the country to a strong economic and social position.

He said that alongside political rights, ensuring people’s economic capability is crucial. To this end, the government will provide all necessary policy support to encourage domestic entrepreneurs in investment and job creation.

The Prime Minister made these remarks on Tuesday (August 11) at a contract signing ceremony for leasing three closed state-owned jute mills to two private companies, held at the Cabinet Division’s conference room in the Secretariat. The Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary, Hasan Shiplu, confirmed this.

Promising to stand by the country’s genuine entrepreneurs, the Prime Minister said that the government would provide them with necessary cooperation. Supporting entrepreneurs would not only create employment and ensure livelihoods for people but also improve the overall economic situation.

The head of government stated, “We aim to build a country where everyone is better off than they are currently. This is our primary goal and objective.”

Emphasizing domestic investment alongside foreign investment, the Prime Minister said that foreign investment is certainly welcome, and the government desires it. However, the country’s own investors and entrepreneurs must also be encouraged. The government will provide all necessary policy support for their businesses and investments.

Highlighting that the core objective of the government’s policy is to create opportunities for people from all walks of life, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said that the government is working to build a beautiful and strong nation with everyone’s cooperation.

The Prime Minister thanked the two business groups that took responsibility for the three mills. He expressed hope that these companies would succeed with their new investments and contribute to the national economy through job creation.

Also speaking at the event were Commerce, Industry, and Textiles & Jute Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, State Minister for Textiles & Jute Shariful Alam, Secretary of Textiles & Jute Sharof Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, Chairman of PRAN-RFL Group Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, and Managing Director of Hamco Group ATM Mostafa.

Senior officials from BJMC and the leased institutions were also present at the event.

item.title: 3 State-Owned Jute Mills to Resume Operation, Creating 11,000 Jobs
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Three large state-owned jute mills, which had been shut down for a long time, are finally set to resume operations under private management. This will create new employment opportunities for…

The post 3 State-Owned Jute Mills to Resume Operation, Creating 11,000 Jobs appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Three large state-owned jute mills, which had been shut down for a long time, are finally set to resume operations under private management. This will create new employment opportunities for approximately 11,629 people.

On Tuesday (August 11), a lease agreement was signed between Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation (BJMC), Pran-RFL Group, and Hamko Group in the Cabinet Division conference room at the Secretariat, in the presence of Prime Minister Tareq Rahman.

According to the agreement, Pran-RFL Group has been awarded the lease for Jatiya Jute Mills Limited in Sirajganj and Star Jute Mills Limited in Khulna. Hamko Group will operate Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills Limited in Khulna.

Brigadier General Md. Kabir Uddin Sikder, Chairman of BJMC, signed the agreement on behalf of the corporation, while representatives from the respective leasing companies signed on their behalf. The Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary, Hasan Shiplu, confirmed this information.

It is understood that private companies will invest approximately BDT 619 crore to resume production in these three factories. This investment is expected to generate a potential annual turnover of around BDT 1,175 crore.

An investment of BDT 157 crore in Jatiya Jute Mill in Raipura, Sirajganj, will create jobs for 5,238 people. Star Jute Mill in Dighelia, Khulna, will see an investment of BDT 250 crore, providing employment for another 5,238 workers. Meanwhile, Platinum Jubilee Jute Mill in Khalishpur, Khulna, will receive an investment of BDT 212 crore, generating 1,153 jobs.

During the signing ceremony, it was announced that the government has decided to lease 20 of BJMC’s 25 closed jute mills to private management. So far, the lease process for 14 mills has been completed, and full-scale production has already begun in 9 factories.

Also present at the event were Commerce, Industry, and Textiles and Jute Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, State Minister for Textiles and Jute Shariful Alam, and other high-ranking officials.

item.title: The Smartest Ways to Keep Trending Videos on Your Device Before They Disappear
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
The digital world moves fast. A video can be popular one moment and then be gone the next. This could be because of privacy changes, copyright claims, sound being turned…

The post The Smartest Ways to Keep Trending Videos on Your Device Before They Disappear appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
The digital world moves fast. A video can be popular one moment and then be gone the next. This could be because of privacy changes, copyright claims, sound being turned off, or the creator taking it down. You might feel annoyed when you wait for a video to load on bad public Wi-Fi. It can also feel tough to find a video that was removed earlier in the week.

Building your own offline media collection is the best way that you can protect your videos from links that stop working and places where the internet does not work well. When you have the videos saved on your device or as files, you will be sure to play them any time. There will not be buffering. You will also keep your videos safe for a long time.

Native Offline Caching Through Official Platform Features

If you want an easy and safe way to use youtube video download on your phone or computer, the app’s built-in offline feature is the best place to start. Streaming platforms have systems that let you save high-quality videos right inside the app. This helps you watch them, even if you lose your connection when you fly, travel, or go somewhere far.

OFFLINE SAVING WORKFLOW

  1. Open video. 2. Tap Action Menu (…) or Download.
  2. Pick video quality (360p / 720p / 1080p)
  3. Get to it with your Profile / Downloads Cache

Key Technical Aspects of Built-In Caching

  • Encrypted Cache Storage: Videos are kept inside the app’s safe file system. They are not in open system folders. This stops files from breaking and lets media stay in sync with creator channel changes.
  • Resolution Management: You can pick standard 360p to save space when you just want to look at videos, or go with 720p or 1080p if you need more detail for guides.
  • 30-Day Check-In Interval: Downloads stay working offline if your device goes online at least one time every 30 days. This lets the app make sure you can use the videos.

Desktop Software Solutions for Local File Retention

If you are a creator, researcher, or someone who loves media, you might want MP4 files saved right on your computer. You may not want them in an app space. A desktop program gives you many ways to get this done. It works very well.

This kind of program is not like saving things on your phone. Standalone software pulls out the real audio and video files. You can put them in folders you make, change them, or move them to other storage drives.

Method Comparison: Caching vs. Direct Storage

Feature Criteria In-App Mobile Caching Desktop Downloader Tools
File Accessibility Encrypted within app Loose MP4/MKV files in local drive
Offline Expiration Requires 30-day sync Permanent storage (No expiration)
Playback Flexibility In-app player only Any media player (VLC, QuickTime)
Network Reliance High-efficiency internal CDN Adjustable bandwidth limits
Subtitles & Audio Tracks Integrated automatically Extracted as separate SRT/MP3 files

Open-Source Network Stream Capture

A vast majority of power users employ popular free software media players like VLC Media Player or yt-dlp. The media player gets the video URL and finds the location within the video stream in the network. This allows the downloading of video directly via the URL without any third-party websites that contain lots of advertising and pop-ups.

Short-form vertical content archiving

At the moment, the development of short-form videos taken in the 9:16 format is progressing at the fastest pace among all types of digital content on the internet.

Such short videos frequently change, blend into each other, or disappear because of the changing tendencies and licensing requirements for soundtracks. The approach of working has to be fast and phone-based.

               [ Trending Short-Form Clip ]

                 │

                 ▼

             Copy Direct Video Link (URL)

                 │

                 ▼

               ┌───────────────────────────┐

       │ Process via Browser Tool  │

                └─────────────┬─────────────┘

                 │

                 ▼

         Select Output Resolution (1080p)

                 │

                 ▼

       Saved to Device Camera Roll / Files

Recommended Steps for Saving Vertical Clips

  1. Find the Share Trigger: Tap the share button on the video screen. Pick “Copy Link” and get the link for this video.
  2. Tools for Privacy Protection: Embed the link in any normal browsing tool or in a phone application such as Seal or any browsing extension that will protect your information.
  3. Aspect Ratio and Resolution: Ensure that your video is still kept in the normal 9:16 format and at the full speed of the video (60 fps when visible).

Best Practices for Managing Local Video Archives

Saving content is important, but there is more to it. You need to sort and keep your digital media safe. This makes sure you can get to your files for years. Sometimes files are gone from public servers, but you will still have them.

  • Standardized Naming Conventions: Set up a simple way to name files. Be sure to include the date they are uploaded, the name of the person who made them, and the main subject. For example: 2026-07_CreatorName_Topic.mp4.
  • Categorized Directory Tree: Put saved videos into clear main folders. Use names like Tutorials, Design Inspiration, News Archives, or Entertainment. This helps and stops your download folders from being messy.
  • Backup Storage Locations: Use the 3-2-1 backup rule. Keep 3 copies of important files. Store them on 2 kinds of storage, like a local NVMe SSD and another hard drive. Keep 1 backup at another site or a safe cloud storage.
  • Storage Space Audits: Check your space often. Remove draft clips that you do not need or extra files. This helps your phone and computer have enough room for videos that matter.

Responsible Content Retaining and Legal Overview

Many people keep local backups of online videos. They do this for their own offline viewing, for learning, or for creative ideas. This is a common practice now. But, it is important to respect the rights of creators and who owns the content.

  • Personal Use Limits: You should keep downloaded media for yourself. Do not use it to make money or share it with others. Only use it offline.
  • Attribution and Permissions: Do not upload, monetize, or distribute the saved clips anywhere else without explicit written permission of the rights owner.
  • Fair Use Conditions: Whenever you look at media that is current and popular to either comment on it, express opinions on it, or even for educational purposes, then you must comply with the fair use requirements established.

Efficient Video Archival Summary

Getting good at a few easy-to-follow habits can help you keep web content, tech guides, and funny moments long after those first links stop working. You might use an app’s caching to stream while you travel, or you could save videos with open-source desktop tools. Choosing the right way helps make sure your top media files are safe and easy for you to view at any time. Since internet stuff comes and goes so fast now, taking just a few more seconds to download youtube shorts and new how-to videos can make sure your favorite things stay on your device when you want them.

item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Prime Minister Tareq Rahman stated that there is currently a favorable investment climate in Bangladesh. He added that the government is ready to provide all kinds of cooperation to interested…

The post Government Ready to Provide All Kinds of Cooperation to Foreign Investors: Prime Minister appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Tareq Rahman stated that there is currently a favorable investment climate in Bangladesh. He added that the government is ready to provide all kinds of cooperation to interested foreign investors.

The Prime Minister made these remarks on Tuesday morning (August 11) during a courtesy call with a delegation from the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham). The Prime Minister’s Assistant Press Secretary, Gazi Shahriar Pamir, confirmed this.

An eight-member delegation, led by AmCham Bangladesh’s President and Mastercard’s Vice President, Syed Mohammad Kamal, met with the Prime Minister.

During the meeting, AmCham representatives informed that the organization’s new committee took charge approximately two months ago. The new committee is working to attract more US investment to Bangladesh and strengthen commercial ties between the two countries.

In response, the Prime Minister reiterated that a favorable investment environment currently prevails in Bangladesh. He assured that the government is ready to provide all necessary cooperation to ensure foreign investors can invest without hindrance.

Also present at the meeting were Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, the Prime Minister’s Advisor for Post, Telecommunication, Information Technology, and Science & Technology Rehan Asif Asad, and the Executive Chairman of Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), Ashik Chowdhury.

item.title: Fascist Government Destroyed Everything, Now It’s Time for Reconstruction: Prime Minister
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman remarked that the fascist government, over more than a decade and a half, has destroyed various sectors of the country, including education, health, and economy. He…

The post Fascist Government Destroyed Everything, Now It’s Time for Reconstruction: Prime Minister appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman remarked that the fascist government, over more than a decade and a half, has destroyed various sectors of the country, including education, health, and economy. He stated that it is now time to reconstruct these sectors, and the current government is working towards that goal.

He made these remarks on Monday (August 10) afternoon at the China-Bangladesh Friendship Conference Centre in the capital, during the inauguration ceremony of activities for three villages under the SDG Village Pilot Program.

On this day, the Prime Minister inaugurated the activities of three villages under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Village Pilot Program, a first for the country. The selected villages are Nafanagar in Bochaganj Upazila, Dinajpur; Pankhali in Dacope Upazila, Khulna; and Mitinggachhari in Kaptai Upazila, Rangamati.

During the event, the Prime Minister stated that a situation of destruction has been created in almost all sectors, including education, health, and economy, over more than a decade and a half. Now, the government is moving forward with the goal of reconstructing these sectors and building the country as a democratic and welfare state.

He added, “SDGs have a crucial role to play in this journey of national reconstruction. It is not possible for any single ministry or department to achieve the SDG targets alone. Cooperation from all relevant parties is required for this.”

Tarique Rahman said that the government’s public policy aligns with the core principle of SDGs, ‘leaving no one behind.’ The government’s objective is to ensure the interests of people from all walks of life in the country. Therefore, the government’s policy is ‘Bangladesh for All.’

The Prime Minister stated that to ensure sustainable development, emphasis is being placed on improving the living standards of people in remote areas, increasing access to education and healthcare, creating employment, and enhancing economic capacity. Through the SDG Village Pilot Program, these initiatives will be coordinated to create an effective development model.

He further added that Bangladesh has shown success in implementing the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). Similarly, Bangladesh is systematically taking and implementing various steps to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, along with other relevant officials, were present at the event.

item.title: Indian High Commissioner Meets Prime Minister to Strengthen Bangladesh-India Ties
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to further strengthen Bangladesh-India bilateral relations. During the meeting, discussions were held on economic cooperation between the…

The post Indian High Commissioner Meets Prime Minister to Strengthen Bangladesh-India Ties appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Indian High Commissioner to Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to further strengthen Bangladesh-India bilateral relations. During the meeting, discussions were held on economic cooperation between the two countries, border management, various issues of mutual interest, and ways to advance bilateral relations in the future.

The meeting took place at the Prime Minister’s Office in the Bangladesh Secretariat on Monday (August 10) at around 11:00 AM.

According to diplomatic sources, the meeting emphasized enhancing economic cooperation between Bangladesh and India, making border management more effective, and strengthening cooperation on issues of mutual interest. Various potential initiatives to further solidify the existing relationship were also discussed.

Earlier on Sunday (August 9), Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi spoke about the future of Bangladesh-India relations at the inauguration of a new play area for children at the Indian Visa Application Centre in Dhaka. He stated that the relationship between the common people of the two countries is very strong and expressed hope that this cordiality would further extend to the governmental level.

Praising Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s leadership, Dinesh Trivedi referred to him as a pro-people leader. He also mentioned that India’s Prime Minister is also pro-people and stated that many complex issues could be resolved through discussions if the heads of government of the two neighboring countries work together.

Furthermore, the Indian High Commissioner also announced initiatives to make Indian visa services in Bangladesh easier and more effective. He informed that various steps are being taken to increase the capacity for receiving and processing visa applications, reduce costs for applicants’ convenience, and improve service quality.

Diplomatic sources indicate that Monday’s meeting emphasized overall aspects of Bangladesh-India bilateral relations, as well as specific issues such as visa services, economic cooperation, and border management.

item.title: “Why Are You Calling It Bad? It’s a Beautiful Result”: Education Minister
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.description:
Despite a decrease in both the pass rate and the number of GPA-5 recipients in this year’s SSC and equivalent examinations, Education Minister Dr. ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon has described…

The post “Why Are You Calling It Bad? It’s a Beautiful Result”: Education Minister appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
item.content:encoded:
Despite a decrease in both the pass rate and the number of GPA-5 recipients in this year’s SSC and equivalent examinations, Education Minister Dr. ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon has described the results as “beautiful.”

He made this remark in response to a question at a press conference held on Monday (August 10) after the announcement of the SSC and equivalent examination results.

This year, the total pass rate for the SSC and equivalent examinations is 62.25 percent. A total of 116,676 students achieved GPA-5. Last year, 139,032 students secured GPA-5, indicating a decrease in the number of GPA-5 recipients compared to the previous year.

When the Education Minister’s attention was drawn to the decline in the pass rate and GPA-5, he urged not to view the matter negatively.

The Education Minister stated, “Why are you calling it bad? It’s a beautiful result.”

He added that during the evaluation of exam scripts, the true achievements of the students were given importance. In this context, he quipped, “You can sing with an open heart, but you cannot give marks with an open heart.”

Despite the decrease in the pass rate and GPA-5 in this year’s results, according to the Education Minister, the outcome should be viewed not merely as a numerical assessment but as a reflection of students’ true merit and competence.

This year, a total of 1,857,344 students filled out forms for the SSC and equivalent examinations. Among them, 1,418,398 students participated in the SSC examinations under nine general education boards, 304,286 in the Dakhil examinations under the Madrasah Education Board, and 134,660 in the SSC (Vocational) examinations under the Technical Education Board.

The post “Why Are You Calling It Bad? It’s a Beautiful Result”: Education Minister appeared first on Bangla Online News Portal.
